quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-01.prompt:
Let $G$ be a group of order $|G| = 504 = 7 \cdot 8 \cdot 9$.

(i) If there exists an element $x \in G$ of order $21$, show that there exists a subgroup $H \subset G$ having index $|G : H| = 8$. *Hint.* Find the possibilities for $n_7$, the number of Sylow 7-subgroups of $G$.

(ii) If $G$ is simple, show that it contains no element of order $21$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-01.answer: (i) $P=\langle x^3\rangle$ is Sylow with $\langle x\rangle\le N_G(P)$, so $n_7\mid24$ and $n_7\equiv1\ (7)$, i.e. $n_7\in\{1,8\}$; take $H=N_G(P)$ if $n_7=8$, and $H=PQ$ ($Q\in\mathrm{Syl}_3$) if $n_7=1$. (ii) Then $G\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sym}_8$, which has no element of order 21 (a 7-cycle and a 3-cycle need 10 points).

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-02.prompt: Let $R$ be a ring and let $M$ be a right $R$-module which has a composition series. Assume that $M$ has a unique simple submodule $N$ and that $N$ is not isomorphic to any composition factor of $M/N$. Prove that the ring $\mathrm{End}_R(M)$ is a division ring. In other words, prove that every nonzero $R$-endomorphism of $M$ is one-to-one and onto.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-02.answer: Every nonzero submodule contains $N$. If $0\ne\theta$ had kernel $K\ne0$, then $N\subseteq K$ and $L=\theta^{-1}(N)$ satisfies $L/K\cong N$, making $N$ a composition factor of $M/N$. So $\theta$ is injective, and then onto by comparing composition lengths.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-03.prompt:
Let $K \subseteq E$ be fields and let $f(x) \in K[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $n \ge 2$ having $n$ distinct roots $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ in $E$. Suppose that the field extension $K[a_1, a_2]/K$ has degree $|K[a_1, a_2] : K| = n(n - 1)$.

(i) Find the degrees of the irreducible factors of $f(x)$ over the field $K$ and over the field $K[a_1]$.

(ii) If $g(x)$ is the minimal polynomial of $a_1 + a_2$ over $K$, prove that $a_i + a_j$ is a root of $g(x)$ for all $i \neq j$. *Hint.* First consider the case $i = 1$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-03.answer: (i) Over $K$, $f$ is irreducible (one factor of degree $n$); over $K[a_1]$, $f=(x-a_1)h(x)$ with $h$ irreducible of degree $n-1$. (ii) The Galois group of $f$ is $2$-transitive on the roots (there are $n(n-1)$ embeddings of $K[a_1,a_2]$), so some automorphism maps $a_1+a_2$ to $a_i+a_j$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-04.prompt: Let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over the integers $\mathbb{Z}$ and consider the system of homogeneous linear equations $AX = 0$ where $X$ is the column vector of unknowns $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Suppose that every integer solution of this system has all $x_i$'s equal. Prove that the same is true for every real solution of this system of equations.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-04.answer: Rational solutions scale to integer solutions, so the rational null space is $0$ or spanned by $(1,\dots,1)^T$; the real null space is spanned by the rational one (row reduction happens over $\mathbb Q$), so every real solution is a multiple of $(1,\dots,1)^T$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-05.prompt:
Let $K = \mathbb{Q}[i]$ be the field generated over the rationals $\mathbb{Q}$ by $i = \sqrt{-1}$ and let $R$ be the subring of $K$ defined by
$$R = \{ a + bi \mid a, b \in \mathbb{Z} \}$$
where $\mathbb{Z}$ is the ring of integers. Suppose $\alpha$ is a complex number which is the root of a monic polynomial in $R[x]$. Prove that the minimal monic polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$ has all coefficients in $R$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1993f-05.answer: $R=\mathbb Z[i]$ is a UFD (Euclidean), hence integrally closed in $K$. The roots of the minimal polynomial $g$ of $\alpha$ over $K$ are roots of the given monic polynomial, hence integral over $R$; the coefficients of $g$ are symmetric functions of them, so integral over $R$ and in $K$, hence in $R$.
